name: Tria Beauty hair removal laser

lead: The Tria is a consumer diode laser for hair removal at home. According to Wikipedia, it is one of two diode devices the US FDA had cleared for over-the-counter sale as of 2025.

Laser hair removal in clinics is described as producing long-term hair reduction rather than total removal, usually needing several sessions. Sources specific to the Tria were limited, so this article is short.

paras: Laser energy is absorbed by melanin in the hair and heats the follicle (selective photothermolysis), damaging it while sparing most surrounding skin. Treatments are repeated over weeks to months.
Common effects are redness, itching and swelling lasting a few days; burns, pigment changes and eye injury are possible. Results vary by hair and skin colour.

lead: The Tria is a hair-removal diode laser sold for home use. Wikipedia states that, as of 2025, the US FDA had cleared two diode devices for over-the-counter sale, the Epilaser and the TRIA. [1]

Professional laser hair removal works by selective photothermolysis: light absorbed by melanin heats the hair follicle. [1] It is cleared for "permanent hair reduction", meaning a long-term decrease in regrowth rather than total removal. [1]

paras: Wavelength and pulse duration are chosen so melanin absorbs most of the energy. Dark, coarse hair on light skin responds best; light, red, grey, white and fine hair respond poorly. [1] Most people need at least eight sessions spaced 3 to 8 weeks apart. [1]

No studies found on the Tria specifically in the sources reviewed. For the category, a randomized trial cited in encyclopedic sources reported 69.2% hair reduction with a diode laser versus 52.7% with IPL at 12 months, [1] and a 2023 PLoS One study compared a home-use laser with a clinical diode laser.

Common short-lived effects include itching, redness and swelling for two or three days; acne and skin discoloration are the most serious common effects, with burns and infection also reported. [1] Review literature notes diode lasers had the most side effects in one comparison. [1]
